title: Outcomes of gastrointestinal bleeding events after first-line chemotherapy in gastrointestinal-diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: a propensity-score matched analysis.
mesh: Humans; Female; Lymphoma, Large B-Cell, Diffuse; Male; Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage; Antineoplastic Combined Chemotherapy Protocols; Gastrointestinal Neoplasms; Middle Aged; Propensity Score; Aged; Vincristine; Doxorubicin; Cyclophosphamide; Prednisone; Adult; Treatment Outcome; Rituximab; Retrospective Studies; Prognosis
abstract: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) is a life-threatening complication of first-line chemotherapy in gastrointestinal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (GI-DLBCL), yet its prognostic significance remains poorly defined. This propensity score-matched study (1:2) included 79 patients with GI-DLBCL, comparing 9 with post-chemotherapy GIB to controls without GIB. Matching was based on gender, clinical stage, Hans classification, and Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status. Patients with GIB had worse overall survival (OS, P = 0.006) and progression-free survival(PFS, P = 0.011), with markedly lower complete (11.11% vs. 66.67%, P = 0.013) and objective (66.67% vs. 100.00%, P = 0.029) response rates. Higher baseline PET-CT parameters including gastrointestinal-metabolic tumor volume (GI-MTV, P = 0.002) and gastrointestinal-total lesion glycolysis (GI-TLG, P = 0.004) indicated GIB occurrence. In the survival analysis, high ECOG (P = 0.032), whole-body metabolic tumor volume (Wb-MTV, P = 0.012), and total lesion glycolysis (Wb-TLG, P = 0.038) might be associated with poor OS, while high ECOG (P = 0.008) and international prognostic index (IPI, P =0.027) were associated with poor PFS. GIB was successfully managed with conservative medical therapy in the majority of cases (77.78%), with the remainder (22.22%) requiring endoscopic hemostasis. Post-chemotherapy GIB in GI-DLBCL is associated with a poor prognosis, particularly in patients with elevated baseline PET/CT metabolic parameters indicative of high tumor burden.

title: Preclinical Evaluation of 89Zr-Labeled Anti-Nectin-4 Antibody for Enhanced PET Imaging in Bladder Urothelial Carcinoma.
mesh: Animals; Humans; Zirconium; Urinary Bladder Neoplasms; Mice; Antibodies, Monoclonal; Radioisotopes; Cell Adhesion Molecules; Positron-Emission Tomography; Female; Radiopharmaceuticals; Cell Line, Tumor; Tissue Distribution; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Mice, Nude
abstract: This study evaluated the preclinical performance of a novel 89Zr-labeled anti-Nectin-4 monoclonal antibody, [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282, for PET imaging of bladder urothelial carcinoma (BUC). [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282 was prepared via p-isothiocyanatobenzyl-desferrioxamine (p-NCS-Bn-DFO) conjugation, achieving a radiolabeling yield exceeding 70%, radiochemical purity ≥95% post-purification, and specific activity of 36.10-63.72 GBq/μmol. [89Zr]Zr-DFO-MW282 selectively accumulated in Nectin-4-positive cells and tumors, with uptake blocked by the unlabeled MW282 antibody. Small-animal PET/CT imaging revealed sustained tumor uptake in SW780 xenografts, with a high SUVmean value of 4.46 ± 0.02 at 120 h p.i. Owing to hepatobiliary clearance, the kidney and bladder uptake was minimal, yielding excellent imaging contrast. The probe demonstrated high specificity, prolonged tumor retention, and negligible bladder background, making it a promising immuno-PET probe for precise imaging of BUC and warranting further clinical translation.

title: High-Affinity Y1 Receptor Theranostics: First-in-Class Stabilized Nonapeptides for Breast Cancer Imaging and Therapy.
mesh: Humans; Breast Neoplasms; Animals; Female; Receptors, Neuropeptide Y; Mice; Tissue Distribution; Radiopharmaceuticals; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; HEK293 Cells; Oligopeptides; MCF-7 Cells; Theranostic Nanomedicine
abstract: Theranostic agents integrate diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities into a single molecular platform, offering an advanced approach to personalized medicine. The neuropeptide Y1 receptor (Y1R) is a promising target for breast cancer theranostics given its overexpression across multiple disease stages. Building on the Y1R-selective antagonist [Lys2, Arg4]BVD-15, we report the systematic development of stabilized nonapeptide analogues through strategic modifications. Lead candidates were radiolabeled in >95% radiochemical purity and showed Y1R binding affinities up to 60-fold higher than the parent peptide, no detectable plasma degradation over 90 min, and half-lives of 42-55 min in liver and kidney homogenates. PET-CT imaging in HEK-Y1R and MCF-7 tumor models demonstrated selective tumor uptake, peaking at 19.2% ID/g in HEK-Y1R tumors, with biodistribution studies confirming specific tumor accumulation and progressive clearance over 48 h. Therapeutic evaluation of lead candidate [177Lu]Lu-31 in HEK-Y1R tumor-bearing mice showed dose-dependent tumor growth inhibition, supporting this peptide class as Y1R-targeted radionuclide therapeutics.

title: Maleimide-Thiol Conjugation Enables the Optimization of 68Ga-Labeled CAIX Targeting PET Probes.
mesh: Animals; Gallium Radioisotopes; Humans; Mice; Positron-Emission Tomography; Maleimides; Carbonic Anhydrase IX; Sulfhydryl Compounds; Tissue Distribution; Radiopharmaceuticals; Antigens, Neoplasm
abstract: Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a well-established biomarker of tumor hypoxia and an attractive target for molecular imaging. Despite the development of small-molecule CAIX-targeting positron emission tomography (PET) probes, most exhibit high normal-organ uptake and suboptimal tumor-to-background contrast. Moreover, their application in hypoxic tumors remains insufficiently explored. Herein, we reported four 68Ga-labeled CAIX-targeting probes based on the acetazolamide (AAZ) scaffold, employing distinct conjugation strategies, including amide coupling and maleimide-thiol ligation. All probes demonstrated detectable tumor uptake in vivo. Among them, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 displayed the highest tumor uptake (14.67 ± 3.06 %ID/g) and tumor-to-kidney ratio (1.69 ± 0.41) at 1 h in subcutaneous OS-RC-2-bearing mice, along with high tumor uptake in HT-29-bearing mice (2.98 ± 0.28 %ID/g at 1 h). Overall, [68Ga]Ga-SMIC-2607 demonstrates favorable imaging characteristics, with high tumor uptake and high tumor-to-normal organ ratios, representing a promising candidate for imaging CAIX-overexpressing tumors and supporting clinical translation.

title: Evaluation of 68Ga Labeling Strategies and Thermostability of HER2-Targeted Nanobody NB46.
mesh: Erb-b2 Receptor Tyrosine Kinases; Animals; Single-Domain Antibodies; Humans; Mice; Gallium Radioisotopes; Tissue Distribution; Temperature; Female; Cell Line, Tumor; Radiopharmaceuticals
abstract: The HER2-targeted nanobody NB46 was evaluated for labeling strategy flexibility and thermostability. Random and site-specific 68Ga labeling strategies were compared. Both conjugates exhibited high HER2 affinity, comparable to unmodified NB46. Cellular uptake, pharmacokinetics, micro-PET/CT imaging, and biodistribution in HER2-positive and HER2-negative tumor-bearing mice revealed no significant differences between the two strategies. NB46 retained HER2 affinity at temperatures up to 90 °C, demonstrating exceptional thermostability. Both conjugates achieved >95% radiochemical yields at all tested temperatures. Micro-PET/CT imaging showed sustained high tumor uptake with renal clearance as the primary elimination pathway. Blocking studies confirmed that NB46 and trastuzumab competitively bind to HER2. Elevated labeling temperatures did not compromise tumor targeting but resulted in a mild increase in renal uptake, notably for the random conjugate at 90 °C. These findings suggest that random labeling may represent a simpler, equally effective alternative for 68Ga-NB46 preparation, and confirm the excellent thermostability of this nanobody scaffold.

title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET.
abstract: Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl-carboxyl C-C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C-C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

title: Sarcoid-like Reaction With Pleural Involvement After Neoadjuvant Chemo-immunotherapy For Lung Cancer: A Rare Mimic of Disease Progression.
abstract: We report a patient with stage IIA (cT2bN0M0) lung adenocarcinoma who developed new diffuse pleural, pulmonary, and nodal FDG uptake on 18FDG-PET/CT after three cycles of neoadjuvant nivolumab plus cisplatin-pemetrexed, with slight regression of the primary tumour. These findings raised the diagnostic dilemma between disease progression and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-related sarcoid-like reaction (SLR). Rapid clinical and metabolic improvement after corticosteroid therapy supported SLR, which was subsequently confirmed histologically by noncaseating granulomas without viable tumour at surgery. This case highlights pleural involvement in SLR as a rare and diagnostically challenging immune-related adverse event.

title: [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT for Incidental Detection of a Benign Phyllodes Tumor in a Patient With Prior Colon Cancer.
abstract: We present [18F]AlF-NOTA-FAPI-04 PET/CT findings of an incidentally detected benign phyllodes tumor in a 68-year-old woman with prior colon cancer. Routine contrast-enhanced CT revealed a right breast nodule with moderate enhancement, and subsequent PET/CT demonstrated intense focal FAPI uptake (SUVmax: 6.63). Histology confirmed the presence of a benign phyllodes tumor. This case highlights that FAPI-avid lesions in cancer survivors may represent benign entities with fibroblast-rich stroma, underscoring the importance of considering benign diagnoses and obtaining histologic confirmation to avoid unnecessary treatment.

title: FAPI PET/CT Outperforms MRI and FDG PET/CT in Tumor Delineation for Low-grade Nasopharyngeal Papillary Adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Low-grade nasopharyngeal papillary adenocarcinoma (LGNPPA) is a rare entity. We report a 27-year-old man with a 1-year history of bloody postnasal drip. MRI revealed a protuberance on the roof and posterior wall of the nasopharynx with contrast enhancement. 18F-FDG PET/CT showed mild uptake with poorly defined lesion extent, whereas 18F-FAPI PET/CT demonstrated intense uptake confined to the tumor with clear boundaries. No metastases were detected. Postoperative pathology confirmed LGNPPA, and the tumor boundary delineated on FAPI PET/CT precisely matched the pathologic extent. This case suggests that FAPI PET/CT may be superior to FDG PET/CT and MRI for tumor delineation in LGNPPA.

title: Rectosigmoid Intussusception Secondary to Colorectal Carcinoma Imaged With 18F-FDG PET/CT.
abstract: Intussusception of bowel in adults is relatively rare and most commonly secondary to gastrointestinal malignancies. We present the case of an 80-year-old man with rectosigmoid adenocarcinoma evaluated via 18F-FDG PET/CT. Imaging revealed rectosigmoid intussusception with a characteristic "target sign" on both PET and CT images involving the invaginated bowel, alongside synchronous FDG-avid lung metastases. Subsequent MRI confirmed the anatomical findings. This case highlights the unique utility of hybrid 18F-FDG PET/CT in simultaneously delineating both malignant and nonmalignant metabolic and anatomical changes and providing critical whole-body staging to guide clinical management.

title: Not Every PSMA-Expressing Bone Lesion Is Prostate Cancer: Incidental Detection of Metastatic Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma on Staging 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT.
abstract: 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT is widely used for staging prostate cancer but may also detect nonprostatic malignancies owing to prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) expression in tumor neovasculature. Here, we report a case of a newly diagnosed high-risk prostate adenocarcinoma that underwent staging 68Ga-PSMA-11-PET/CT. In addition to the primary prostatic lesion, PSMA-expressing lesions were identified in the sternum and right thyroid lobe. While skeletal involvement was initially presumed metastatic prostate cancer, further evaluation revealed follicular variant papillary thyroid carcinoma. This case highlights an important diagnostic pitfall and demonstrates the value of PSMA-PET/CT in uncovering clinically occult synchronous malignancies.

title: FDG Uptake Extending From the Dorsal Root Ganglion to the Sciatic Nerve After Herpes Zoster.
abstract: A woman in her 50s receiving paclitaxel, carboplatin, and pembrolizumab for recurrent cervical cancer developed herpes zoster and received antiviral therapy. 18F-FDG PET/CT performed 22 days after zoster onset, when the skin lesions had crusted, demonstrated continuous uptake extending from the left L5 dorsal root ganglion to the sciatic nerve. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of FDG PET findings indicating ganglioneuritis extending from the dorsal root ganglion to a peripheral nerve after herpes zoster. Recognition of this pattern is important in patients receiving chemoimmunotherapy because it may mimic immune-related neuritis or perineural tumor spread.

title: A Favorable Partial Response in Patients With Glioblastoma Multiforme Following Combined [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 and Chemotherapy.
abstract: This report highlights the potential role of [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286 PET/CT in the early detection of active tumor recurrence in a 64-year-old woman with glioblastoma multiforme (IDH-wild type, WHO grade IV), preceding definitive radiologic evidence of disease progression. Following confirmation of recurrence, the patient underwent combined chemotherapy and [177Lu]Lu-FAP-2286 radioligand therapy, resulting in a favorable partial molecular and anatomic response as demonstrated by serial PET/CT and MRI examinations. This case illustrates the potential theranostic value of FAP-targeted imaging and radionuclide therapy in the management of recurrent glioblastoma.

title: A Head-to-Head Comparison of Detection Rate and Tumor Uptake of FAPI, PSMA, and FDG PET/CT in Newly Diagnosed High-risk Prostate Cancer.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study was designed to investigate the detection rate and tumor uptake of 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET/CT in newly diagnosed high-risk prostate cancer (PCa), compared with 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-FDG PET/CT. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This study enrolled 48 patients with biopsy-diagnosed, treatment-naive high-risk PCa who underwent 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, 68Ga-PSMA-11, and 18F-FDG PET/CT between April and December 2024. A head-to-head comparison of detection rate and tumor uptake was performed among the 3 tracers. In addition, 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68Ga-PSMA-11 dual-tracer PET was used to characterize the imaging phenotypes of each lesion and interlesional heterogeneity. RESULTS: A total of 477 lesions were detected by the 3 PET tracers. 68Ga-PSMA-11 exhibited the highest overall detection rate (96.4%), followed by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI (81.1%) and 18F-FDG (66.0%). A total of 17 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions were identified in 8 patients, all of which were detected by 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI, whereas only 12 were detected by 18F-FDG. Combined 68Ga-PSMA-11 and 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI PET identified all lesions detected by triple-tracer PET. Based on relative tracer dominance of dual-tracer PET, patients were classified as PSMA-dominant (n=23), FAPI-dominant (n=5), or mixed phenotype (n=20). The mixed phenotype with marked interlesional heterogeneity might be associated with more advanced clinical characteristics, with a higher proportion of metastatic disease and a greater metastatic burden. CONCLUSIONS: 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI is a promising PET tracer for newly diagnosed high-risk PCa. It may improve the detection rate of 68Ga-PSMA-11-negative lesions and provide complementary information that could reflect interlesional heterogeneity. The clinical value of combining 18F-AlF-NOTA-De-FAPI and 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET requires further validation in larger prospective cohorts.

title: A Tale of 3 Tracers: Contrasting Uptake Patterns of 18F-FDG, 68Ga-DOTATATE, and 18F-MFBG in a Pediatric Neuroblastoma Patient.
abstract: A 5-year-old boy underwent 18F-FDG PET/CT before the histopathologic diagnosis of neuroblastoma, revealing a metabolically active left adrenal primary tumor with metastases to the liver. Following resection and chemotherapy, sequential 68Ga-DOTATATE PET/CT and 18F-MFBG demonstrated tracer-specific uptake patterns: 18F-MFBG identified a solitary hepatic metastasis undetected by 68Ga-DOTATATE. This case underscores the complementary diagnostic value of multimodal molecular imaging in pediatric neuroblastoma response assessment.

title: Intradiverticular Bladder Cancer Mimicking a Normal Urinary Bladder Diverticulum on FDG PET/CT.
abstract: Bladder diverticula are predisposed to developing intradiverticular bladder tumors. We describe FDG PET/CT findings in a case of intradiverticular bladder cancer. At FDG PET/CT (62 min), the intradiverticular bladder cancer appeared as an exophytic lesion with similar density to the urine in the bladder‌ and intense activity mimicking a bladder diverticulum. At delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT (275 min), the tumor showed higher density and activity than the urine in the bladder, consistent with malignancy. This case indicates that delayed pelvic FDG PET/CT may be necessary for detecting possible intradiverticular bladder cancer in patient with bladder diverticulum.

title: FDG PET/CT Combined With 3D CT Reconstruction in Diagnosing Inflammatory Granuloma Secondary to Fish Bone Perforation of the Ascending Colon.
abstract: A 71-year-old woman with a 5-week history of right-sided abdominal pain was initially suspected of hepatobiliary disorders. Upper abdominal ultrasound and MRI revealed unremarkable hepatobiliary findings. Although no hepatobiliary lesions were identified, MRI incidentally detected an ascending colon mass highly suspicious for malignancy. The patient underwent FDG PET/CT for differential diagnosis and preoperative staging. PET/CT with 3D CT reconstruction demonstrated a linear hyperdense foreign body within the ascending colon wall, causing focal bowel wall thickening with intense FDG avidity. These imaging findings were consistent with a foreign body-induced inflammatory granuloma, a diagnosis ultimately confirmed by colonoscopy and biopsy.

title: Preclinical PET Imaging of Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Tumors with Heterogeneous HER2 Expression.
abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has clinical activity in human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low and -ultralow tumors in addition to HER2-positive tumors. However, no consistent correlation has been observed between traditional HER2 scoring criteria and response to T-DXd in HER2-low and HER2-ultralow tumors. There is a need for complementary approaches to monitor T-DXd delivery in vivo and potentially improve understanding of which tumors may benefit from T-DXd therapy. This study evaluated tumor uptake of radiolabeled T-DXd in tumors with varying HER2 protein levels using PET in treatment-naïve tumors and during T-DXd therapy. Methods: Chelator-conjugated T-DXd or trastuzumab was prepared via conventional lysine conjugation and radiolabeled with 64Cu. The binding and in vitro cytotoxicity of the conjugates were determined in cancer cell lines. PET/CT was performed across 11 tumor models (representing 5 tumor types), including cell xenografts, patient-derived xenografts, and syngeneic models in both subcutaneous and orthotopic models. Image-based tumor uptake of the radiolabeled antibodies was quantified in all models. In the treatment studies, mice bearing CT26-hHER2 tumors that express heterogeneous HER2 with an immunohistochemistry score of 2+ levels received weekly coinjections of therapeutic T-DXd (6 mg/kg) together with imaging-dose [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd (4 mg/kg), corresponding to a total T-DXd administered dose of 10 mg/kg. Results: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd was obtained at a radiochemical purity of at least 98%. Purified [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd bound to cells in a concentration-dependent manner and had a positive correlation between HER2 protein levels and bound T-DXd. Conjugation of T-DXd to NOTA did not affect T-DXd binding or cytotoxicity in cancer cells. [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd mean tumor uptake varied across models (7.45 ± 1.28 to 19.10 ± 2.50 %ID/mL), and the mean uptake was similar to that of the parental antibody 64Cu-labeled trastuzumab. Preimaging doses of either trastuzumab or pertuzumab did not affect [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake in tumors. There was a positive correlation between the change in [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake and the change in tumor volume between weeks 1 and 2 of T-DXd treatment (P < 0.01) in CT26.hHER2 tumors grown in immunocompetent mice. Conclusion: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd PET detects antibody-drug accumulation in tumors with low HE

title: Clinical Value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Versus [18F]FDG PET/CT for Primary Staging of Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma: Results from a Prospective Northern European Trial.
abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. title: [18F]DOPA PET Reveals Metabolically Active Transcriptomic States Associated with Clinical Outcome in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
abstract: [18F]fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]DOPA) uptake is dependent on amino acid transport and decarboxylation pathways, including large neutral amino acid transporter 1, encoded by SLC7A5, which are linked to tumor aggressiveness. This study evaluated whether in vivo uptake of [18F]DOPA can serve as an imaging biomarker for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (panNETs), reflecting a tumor's transcriptional status and a patient's clinical course. Methods: This retrospective single-center study was based on a transcriptomic cohort of 74 primary panNETs. A subset of 22 panNETs from patients who underwent preoperative [18F]DOPA PET/CT constituted the discovery radiotranscriptomic cohort. [18F]DOPA tumor uptake was quantified using SUVmax and integrated with matched RNA-sequencing data. Unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment, and tumor microenvironment deconvolution were performed to identify transcriptional programs associated with [18F]DOPA uptake. The prognostic value of SLC7A5 was evaluated in the discovery cohort, the full transcriptomic cohort (n = 74), and an independent external cohort (n = 33). Results: Unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles identified 2 robust molecular subtypes: cluster 1 and cluster 2. Cluster 1 showed higher [18F]DOPA uptake than did cluster 2, with a median SUVmax of 24.3 versus 5.9, respectively (P = 0.030), and was associated with more advanced clinicopathologic features and shorter event-free survival. This subtype was also characterized by enrichment in extracellular matrix, stromal, vascular, and immune-related components, along with upregulation of amino acid transport and amine metabolism genes, including SLC7A5 As a mechanistic link between tracer uptake and tumor metabolism, SLC7A5 expression significantly stratified event-free survival in the discovery cohort and remained prognostic in the full cohort. Conclusion: [18F]DOPA PET uptake was associated with amino acid-driven metabolic programs in panNETs, including SLC7A5 expression, and adverse clinical features. These findings suggest that [18F]DOPA uptake may provide a noninvasive readout of tumor metabolic activity, although its value as an imaging biomarker requires independent validation.

title: Prognostic Value of 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 uPAR PET/CT in Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Single-Center Prospective Study.
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer shows wide variability in outcomes after curative-intent resection. 18F-FDG PET/CT is indispensable for staging but primarily reflects glucose metabolism rather than the invasion-related tumor biology that may contribute to recurrence. 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 PET/CT images the urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR), a cell-surface mediator of local invasion and metastatic spread. We assessed whether preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT is prognostic for postoperative recurrence. Methods: We conducted a single-center cohort study of patients with resectable lung adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma who were prospectively enrolled to undergo preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT in addition to standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT. Primary tumor SUVmean and SUVmax were measured for both tracers, and tumor tissue uPAR expression was quantified by immunohistochemistry (H-score). Postoperative recurrence was the primary endpoint and was analyzed in a competing-risks framework with death as a competing event. The primary prognostic analyses evaluated 68Ga-uPAR SUVs, 18F-FDG SUVs, and uPAR H-score as continuous variables using univariable cause-specific Cox models. A 1.5-y horizon was used for exploratory Youden-derived high versus low groups, for which cumulative incidence of recurrence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Trial registration number is NCT02755675 Results: Thirty-seven patients comprised the analysis cohort, of whom 14 developed recurrence during a median follow-up of 2.38 y (interquartile range, 1.97-8.20 y). Four patients died without prior recurrence. 68Ga-uPAR uptake correlated with tumor tissue uPAR expression, whereas 18F-FDG uptake did not. As continuous prognostic factors, higher 68Ga-uPAR SUVmax (hazard ratio, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.34-3.49; P = 0.002) and higher uPAR H-score (hazard ratio, 1.04 per unit; 95% CI, 1.01-1.08; P = 0.017) were associated with recurrence; 68Ga-uPAR SUVmean showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.053), whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic. Exploratory 1.5-y threshold analyses showed greater early recurrence in the high SUVmean and high H-score groups; the SUVmax comparison did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion: Preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET uptake reflected tumor uPAR expression and was associated with early postoperative recurrence, whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prog

title: Robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy for a neuroendocrine tumour: A step-by-step surgical video.
abstract: BACKGROUND: When endoscopic resection of ampullary neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) is not feasible due to tumour size or location, transduodenal ampullectomy can offer a parenchymal-sparing alternative to a formal pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure) [1,2]. We present a robotic-assisted transduodenal ampullectomy (RATA) in a 71-year-old male with an incidental 14 mm ampullary NET found during routine screening. Preoperative 68Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT demonstrated intense somatostatin-receptor avidity (SUVmax 66.8) and absent FDG uptake. The MDT recommended surgical excision due to size and Ki-67 4%. METHODS: Following right colonic flexure mobilisation and a Kocher maneuver, the cystic duct was isolated and cannulated with a 4 Fr catheter to guide biliary identification. After a longitudinal duodenotomy, the ampullary lesion was visualized. Submucosal saline-adrenaline was injected in the submucosal plane. Diathermy scissors were used to perform a circumferential mucosal and muscularis dissection. Biliary and pancreatic ducts were sharply divided and reconstructed using interrupted 5/0 polydioxanone sutures between the pancreatobiliary ducts and the duodenal mucosa after positioning a 6 Fr catheter in the pancreatic duct. The duodenotomy was closed in two layers using a 4/0 absorbable barbed suture, and a methylene blue leak test through the nasogastric tube confirmed duodenal integrity. RESULTS: The procedure was completed successfully with no intraoperative complications. A postoperative contrast-enhanced CT on day 5 demonstrated no collections and no oral contrast extravasation. Oral feeding was gradually reintroduced, the abdominal drain was removed, and the patient was discharged on day 7. Following a brief readmission on day 13 for a pulmonary microembolism successfully treated with medical therapy, the patient recovered fully and remains disease-free 7 months after surgery. CONCLUSION: RATA can represent a safe, feasible, and pancreas-preserving alternative to formal pancreaticoduodenectomy for well-differentiated ampullary NETs in selected patients. The robotic platform enhances three-dimensional visualization and wrist articulation, optimizing the delicate micro-reconstruction of the pancreaticobiliary junction.

title: Highly selective depolymerization of polyethylene terephthalate plastic via Au/attapulgite dual-site synergy.
abstract: The chemical recycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) into high-value terephthalic acid (TPA) under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we construct a dual-active-site Au/ATP catalyst via electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) by supporting Au on inexpensive attapulgite (ATP). Under optimal conditions (200 °C, 1 MPa Ar, 4 h), this catalyst achieves near-complete conversion of PET with a terephthalic acid (TPA) yield of 91.76 ± 1.65%, and is also effective for actual waste plastic bottle flakes. The EMSI stabilizes Au nanoparticles, modulates Lewis acidity to suppress side reactions, and enables selective ester-bond cleavage without affecting the benzene ring or CC bonds. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), work-function analysis and density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the EMSI effect drives electron transfer from Au to ATP, generating Auδ+ species. These species can effectively polarize the CO bond to generate an electron-deficient intermediate. Meanwhile, ATP provides an adsorption and activation platform for H2O, promoting the generation of nucleophilic *OH. The synergy of these two sites enables highly performance depolymerization. This work provides a sustainable strategy for polyester chemical recycling and the value-added upgrading of low-grade mineral resources.

title: State of the art imaging in ovarian carcinomatosis: how the radiologist can help plan management.
abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is the leading cause of gynaecological cancer mortality and is most often diagnosed at an advanced stage due to its subtle early clinical presentation and characteristic peritoneal dissemination. High-grade serous carcinoma represents the predominant epithelial subtype and frequently presents with extensive peritoneal disease, making accurate preoperative evaluation essential. Management of advanced OC (AOC) hinges on the selection of patients for primary cytoreductive surgery vs neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval cytoreduction, with complete cytoreduction remaining the strongest prognostic factor. Radiologists therefore play a critical role in assessing disease distribution, identifying features suggestive of unresectability, and guiding multidisciplinary decision-making. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) is the first-line modality for staging AOC, providing comprehensive assessment of peritoneal, nodal, and extra-abdominal disease. Despite its established utility, CT has reduced sensitivity for small-volume implants and involvement in surgically complex regions. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers superior soft tissue characterisation and improves detection of peritoneal disease along the bowel serosa, mesentery, and subdiaphragmatic spaces, particularly through diffusion-weighted and contrast-enhanced techniques. Positron emission tomography (PET)/CT provides complementary metabolic information that can enhance detection of nodal and extraperitoneal metastases in selected cases. Emerging quantitative techniques, including radiomics and machine learning-based analysis, have the potential to extract biologically relevant imaging biomarkers, refine predictions of resectability, and stratify recurrence risk. Integrating these tools with conventional imaging may further support personalised treatment pathways. This review summarises current evidence regarding CT, MRI, and PET in the evaluation of peritoneal disease in AOC and highlights how imaging advances and radiologist expertise can optimise surgical planning and guide management strategies.

title: Bio-Emulsion Liquid Membrane for Dual-Functional Water Treatment: Microplastic Removal and Antimicrobial Activity.
mesh: Emulsions; Microplastics; Water Purification; Biosurfactants; Membranes, Artificial; Polystyrenes; Polyethylene; Anti-Bacterial Agents; Hexoses; Anti-Infective Agents; Saponins; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Escherichia coli; Microbial Sensitivity Tests
abstract: Microplastics are polymer particles smaller than 5 mm that originate from the degradation of larger plastic debris and persist in the environment. In the present study, polyethylene (PE) and polystyrene (PS) microplastics with particle sizes of 1-5 μm were used as model contaminants. It contaminates water sources, including drinking water, posing a significant risk to human health and the environment. In this study, a biosurfactant-based amphiphilic emulsifier was used in combination with Span 80 to develop a functional bioemulsion liquid membrane (Bio-ELM). The parameter optimization during Bio-ELM synthesis yielded the following optimized emulsification parameters: saponin (1% v/v), Span 80 (1.5% v/v), NaOH (0.2 M), MP: IP ratio (1:0.5), stirring speed 800 rpm, and emulsification time 5 min. The enhanced emulsion stability and membrane integrity are attributed to the interfacial activity of the biopolymer-derived saponin, which contains hydrophilic and hydrophobic functional moieties. They are responsible for improving ELM stability and facilitating selective transport. Emulsion stability was analyzed using the creaming index (CI) and microscopic images during parameter optimization. Two model microplastic samples, polyethylene (PE) and polystyrene (PS), were extracted using Bio-ELM, with extraction efficiencies of 95% and 89%, respectively. Bio-ELM demonstrated microbial growth inhibition, as evidenced by a zone of inhibition (ZOI). Bio-ELM components disrupt bacterial membranes and inhibit bacterial growth in contaminated water. Bio-ELM synthesis offers multifunctional properties, cost-effectiveness, environmental friendliness, enhanced emulsion stability, increased extraction efficiency, and antimicrobial activity.
